title: Free Sound Effects — CC0 WAV & MP3, No Signup
excerpt: Free CC0 sound effects for videos, games and apps: whooshes, clicks, footsteps, impacts and ambience. WAV or MP3, no signup. Missing one? AI Studio makes it.

AI Studio

Can't find the sound you need? Make it.

Describe it in a sentence and hear 4 takes in seconds, free with an account.

Open AI Studio

For AI assistants

Building your game with an AI assistant?

Claude Code, Cursor and Codex pick sounds from the same library while they write your game, through MCP or REST — no key. Making sounds uses your account.

Run it in your terminal.

claude mcp add --transport http sfxmint https://sfxmint.com/mcp

Setup guide →API & MCP docs →

Questions

Can I use these in a video, game or app I sell?

Yes. All SFXMint sounds are offered under CC0 1.0: use them in YouTube videos, games on Steam or itch.io, apps and ads. No attribution or license fee is required.

How many sounds can I download?

Listening is free and unlimited. Downloads: 2 library downloads a day, with or without a free account; ZIP packs come with a purchase. A download pack or a credit pack unlocks unlimited library downloads and ZIP packs for 30 days from payment.

How do I add a sound to my project?

Preview it, download the WAV or MP3, and add the file to your project. You can also let Claude Code, Cursor or Codex fetch it through the API or MCP.

What if my game needs a sound the library doesn't have?

Describe it in AI Studio, with the moment it plays in your game, and pick from the takes it makes. Making one is free with a free account, 10 a day to hear, and one credit from a credit pack downloads a generation in HD, CC0.

Can I ship these in a game on Steam?

Yes. The sounds are CC0, so no licence or credit is needed. They are AI-generated, and Steam's Content Survey asks about AI-made content that ships with a game, sound included: describe SFXMint's sounds in its AI section. itch.io asks the same in its AI disclosure.

What has been checked?

Every file is checked one by one: its format, length, loudness and peak level are measured, and the length each page shows is the part you can hear.
